prompt:
Write a single self-contained Python script that implements an optimizer for the GuacaMol Valsartan_SMARTS benchmark (goal-directed generation: satisfy a fixed SMARTS substructure AND match a set of physicochemical targets).

Task
- Your script will be executed ONCE against a fixed objective. There is no similarity constraint. A reference molecule (Valsartan) is provided via AGENT4S_INPUT_JSON['reference_smiles']; it already satisfies the SMARTS requirement and is a natural starting seed for motif-preserving edit search. Final submissions that equal the reference are excluded from scoring, so your outputs must differ from Valsartan in at least one atom.
- Design molecules that (a) contain the Valsartan amide-biphenyl SMARTS motif and (b) simultaneously match the oracle's preferred logP, TPSA, and Bertz complexity windows (the windows are anchored on Sitagliptin's physicochemistry — call the oracle to learn what passes).

Structural requirement (from Valsartan)
- Every candidate MUST contain the substructure SMARTS `CN(C=O)Cc1ccc(c2ccccc2)cc1`. This pattern is interpreted by RDKit as any tertiary amide whose nitrogen carries (a) some aliphatic carbon, (b) any acyl group (C=O; the oxo-carbon may be further substituted, so pentanoyl / formyl / acetyl etc. all match), and (c) a methylene linker to a para-substituted biphenyl — i.e. Valsartan's characteristic biphenyl-methylene-amide motif. When this motif is absent, the oracle returns exactly 0.0 and the candidate cannot succeed.

Execution environment
- Your script will be invoked as `python agent_solution.py` by a subprocess runner.
- It must run CPU-only. Do NOT call .cuda(), .to('cuda'), or any torch.cuda API.
- Wall-clock timeout: 1800 seconds / 30 minutes (see constraints.timeout_seconds).
- You may import: rdkit, numpy, scipy, networkx, pandas, sklearn, stdlib.
- You MAY NOT import: requests, urllib, http, socket, openai, anthropic, google.
- Do NOT download files, load remote model weights, or open network sockets.

Inputs
- Read task input from env var AGENT4S_INPUT_JSON (a JSON object). Fields:
    reference_smiles : str   - Valsartan SMILES. Matches the required SMARTS by construction, so it is a natural seed for local edit search. Submitted analogs equal to the reference are excluded from scoring.
    smarts_pattern   : str   - required substructure SMARTS (`CN(C=O)Cc1ccc(c2ccccc2)cc1`)
    target_score_min : float - minimum Valsartan_SMARTS oracle score for success (0.5)
    oracle_budget    : int   - hard cap on oracle calls (100)

Oracle (your ONLY scoring tool)
- Purpose. The oracle is your single, local scoring interface. It judges one candidate SMILES against the fixed reference molecule and reports whether that candidate satisfies the task. Any SMILES you do NOT pass to oracle.score(...) is invisible to the harness; local RDKit scoring alone is not enough.
- There is no other scoring function to call. Do NOT attempt to import or invoke any module under scorers/ other than the oracle below.
- Background. The Valsartan_SMARTS oracle is TDC Oracle("Valsartan_SMARTS"), a [0, 1] score combining four components non-additively: a binary SMARTS-match gate (the motif above; absent ⇒ 0) and three Gaussian windows on logP, TPSA, and Bertz complexity centered on Sitagliptin-like values. Because the components combine geometrically, a near-zero on ANY one drives the whole score toward zero — so candidates must satisfy ALL four simultaneously. The exact target values and Gaussian widths are NOT disclosed; probe them by spending oracle budget on candidates with varied physicochemistry. Reference points: Valsartan itself scores ≈ 0 (SMARTS present but properties off-target); Sitagliptin scores exactly 0 (SMARTS absent). Nontrivial analogs at the intersection of the two are required.

- Construction (free; no budget cost):
    from scorers.oracle_budget_valsartan_smarts import BudgetedValsartanSMARTSOracle, OracleBudgetExceededError
    oracle = BudgetedValsartanSMARTSOracle(reference_smiles, budget=oracle_budget)
    # smarts_pattern and target_score_min default to the task's values.
  Precomputed reference attributes (free):
    oracle.reference_canonical     : str   - canonical SMILES of the reference (Valsartan)
    oracle.reference_oracle_score  : float - Valsartan_SMARTS score of the reference
    oracle.calls_remaining         -> int

- Call:   result = oracle.score(candidate_smiles)

- Input to score():
    candidate_smiles : str - any SMILES string; invalid, duplicate, or empty
                             inputs are handled gracefully (still cost 1 unit).

- Output dict returned by score():
    valid             : bool       - RDKit could parse the canonicalized SMILES
    canonical_smiles  : str|None   - canonical form of the input
    duplicate         : bool       - same canonical as a previous score() call
    equals_reference  : bool       - canonical == oracle.reference_canonical
    oracle_score      : float|None - Valsartan_SMARTS [0, 1] score
    smarts_ok         : bool       - required SMARTS motif is present
    logp              : float|None - RDKit MolLogP of the candidate
    tpsa              : float|None - RDKit TPSA of the candidate
    bertz             : float|None - RDKit BertzCT complexity
    improved_ok       : bool       - oracle_score >= target_score_min
    success           : bool       - improved_ok AND NOT equals_reference
    calls_used        : int        - budget units spent so far (incl. this call)
    budget            : int        - total allowed (= oracle_budget)
    error             : str|None   - populated on invalid / failed input

- Cost and determinism:
    - Every score() call costs exactly 1 unit - including invalid, duplicate, and empty inputs.
    - score() is deterministic: the same canonical SMILES returns the same result (but still costs 1 unit).
    - When the budget is exhausted, further calls raise OracleBudgetExceededError. Check oracle.calls_remaining first, or wrap calls in try/except.

- You may use RDKit directly for any local operation (parsing, substructure checks, fingerprints, similarity, fragment edits, descriptors). Only oracle.score(...) counts against the budget.

Objective details
- Every submitted candidate MUST contain the required SMARTS motif; those that don't will score 0 and cannot succeed.
- The four oracle components combine geometrically — a candidate that hits the SMARTS and lands close to the oracle's preferred logP / TPSA / Bertz values is the shape of a winner.
- A candidate is considered successful when its Valsartan_SMARTS oracle score is >= target_score_min.

Allowed optimizer families (pick one or combine)
- Fragment assembly around the fixed SMARTS motif (decorate the motif with side chains chosen from BRICS, RECAP, or a custom fragment library)
- Reaction-SMARTS-driven enumeration that guarantees motif preservation
- Local edit search (atom/bond/ring mutations) that rejects any edit breaking the SMARTS match
- Beam search, simulated annealing, or hill-climbing guided by a local surrogate fit to the oracle scores you observe
- Bayesian optimization or bandit search over a discrete motif-preserving edit space
- Multi-objective / Pareto search over (logP, TPSA, Bertz) computed locally with RDKit, then probing the oracle to learn its preferred region

Disallowed
- Training a neural generator (VAE / RL / diffusion) inside the script
- Loading pretrained neural-network weights from disk or the network
- Exhaustive enumeration of all SMILES strings

Implementation warning — molecular assembly
- Do NOT assemble SMILES by f-string / format-template concatenation of fragment strings with ring-closure digits (e.g. `f"{acyl}N(Cc1ccc(-c2ccccc2{ortho})cc1){alpha}"`). Reused digits `c1` / `c2` / `c3` across the template and the inserted fragments collide and produce invalid SMILES at scale — a prior attempt generated 87,906 candidates this way and every single one failed RDKit parsing or the SMARTS check.
- Instead, use RDKit to construct analogs: (a) parse `reference_smiles` to an RWMol and edit atoms/bonds one at a time, re-canonicalizing and re-checking `mol.HasSubstructMatch(Chem.MolFromSmarts(smarts_pattern))` after each edit; or (b) use reaction SMARTS via `AllChem.ReactionFromSmarts` for motif-preserving transformations (substitute a side chain, swap an ortho substituent, extend an alkyl tail); or (c) BRICS decomposition of the reference and re-assembly with `BRICS.BRICSBuild`, filtering to keep only products where the SMARTS still matches. In all cases verify the SMARTS match on the constructed Mol object, not on the raw SMILES string.

How your submission is finalized (you do NOT need to print anything)
- Every `oracle.score(...)` call is automatically appended as one JSON line to the harness's optimizer stream. You do not manage this file yourself.
- After your script exits (or hits the timeout), the harness looks at every candidate you passed to `oracle.score(...)`, keeps the successes (valid SMILES with the required SMARTS motif AND Valsartan_SMARTS oracle score >= target_score_min, excluding the reference), sorts them by oracle score descending, and retains the top 10 as your final submission.
- Duplicates and invalids still consume budget but are filtered out for free. You do NOT need to deduplicate, rank, or print a final list - just call `oracle.score(...)` on the candidates you want evaluated.
- stdout is ignored. Use stderr for any debugging / logging.

Required docstring
- The top of your file must be a one-paragraph docstring naming the algorithm you chose and the key hyperparameters (population size, fragment library size, mutation rate, beam width, etc.).

metadata.notes: Code-optimizer redesign of des_04 (Valsartan_SMARTS). The LLM writes a Python optimizer that searches SMARTS-constrained analogs under a budgeted Valsartan_SMARTS oracle; the harness recovers the top 10 successful analogs from the oracle stream and scores them with a des_04 optimization scorer. Static task — no lead sweep. Requires backing modules scorers/oracle_budget_valsartan_smarts.py and scorers/valsartan_smarts_scorer.py (score_valsartan_smarts_optimization); these need to be authored to match the BudgetedOracleBase / *_optimization scorer pattern used by des_01/03/05/06/07.
